Here is a compact digest of important developments in AI training data licensing deals, content partnerships, and lawsuits from the last 14 days:

1.  **Round Hill Music Sues Suno and Anthropic for Copyright Infringement**
    Independent music publisher Round Hill Music filed two separate copyright lawsuits on August 17, 2026, against AI firms Suno and Anthropic. The lawsuits allege that both companies illegally trained their AI models on Round Hill's copyrighted music and lyrics, including popular songs, by scraping content from the open web without permission or license. Round Hill is seeking over $1 billion in damages and has also accused Suno of Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) violations, naming data-scraping firm Bright Data as a co-defendant in the Suno suit.

2.  **Brazilian Newspaper Folha Settles Lawsuit with OpenAI and Signs Deal with Google**
    Brazilian newspaper Folha has settled its copyright lawsuit against OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, by entering into an agreement with the AI company. This settlement follows closely on the heels of Folha announcing a separate content licensing deal with Google. The specifics of both agreements were not immediately disclosed, but they represent a trend of publishers seeking compensation and control over their content used in AI training.

3.  **Microsoft Secures Content Deal with Australia's Nine Entertainment**
    Microsoft has signed its first content licensing deal for news in the Asia Pacific region with Australia's Nine Entertainment. This partnership allows Microsoft to access Nine Entertainment's content, likely for training its AI models and enhancing its AI-powered services. The terms of the agreement were not publicly disclosed.

4.  **Judge Largely Rejects Perplexity's Motion to Dismiss Reddit's Copyright Lawsuit**
    A federal judge on July 31, 2026, largely rejected an attempt by Perplexity and SerpApi to dismiss a copyright lawsuit filed by Reddit. Reddit's lawsuit, originally filed in October of the previous year, accuses Perplexity and three data-scraping suppliers (SerpApi, Oxylabs, and AWMProxy) of "industrial-scale" bypassing of technical protections to obtain Reddit content for Perplexity's AI answer engine. The judge's ruling indicates that Reddit has plausibly argued that Perplexity conspired with at least one of the data scrapers to bypass access controls and acquire Reddit's material.

## Cited sources
1. [forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/virginieberger/2026/08/26/round-hill-sues-suno-anthropic---illegally-scraped-music-isnt-fair-use/)
2. [pressgazette.co.uk](https://pressgazette.co.uk/platforms/news-publisher-ai-deals-lawsuits-openai-google/)

Here is a compact digest of important developments concerning AI training data licensing deals, content partnerships, or lawsuits from the last 14 days (April 5 - April 19, 2026):

1.  **HarperCollins Partners with Toonstar for AI-Generated YouTube Shorts**
    HarperCollins has entered into a new content partnership with Toonstar to transform traditional book titles into AI-generated YouTube Shorts. This collaboration aims to bring books to a wider audience through short-form video content.
2.  **Perplexity Accused of Sharing User Conversations in New Lawsuit**
    AI engine Perplexity is facing a new lawsuit alleging that it shared user conversations with Meta and Google. This legal action raises concerns about data privacy and the handling of user interactions by AI platforms.
3.  **Nota News Plagiarism Findings Lead to Client Reviews**
    An investigation by Poynter, published on April 17, 2026, revealed extensive plagiarism on Nota's AI-powered local news sites, leading to the company closing the sites and some clients reviewing their relationships with Nota. This incident highlights significant issues regarding AI-generated content integrity and journalistic ethics.
4.  **Arc XP Integrates TollBit to Facilitate Publisher Licensing to AI**
    Arc XP has integrated TollBit to provide a mechanism for mid-size publishers to charge AI bots for access to their content. The Philadelphia Inquirer is reportedly planning to adopt this integration, offering a new model for content monetization in the AI era.
5.  **USPTO Introduces New AI Enhancements for Trademark Search**
    The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) announced new artificial intelligence enhancements, including a beta image-search capability within its trademark search system and a mark description and color claim generator for the Trademark Center. These tools aim to modernize trademark examination and improve searchability and application quality.
6.  **White House Framework Recommends AI Licensing and Digital Replica Protections**
    While released on March 20, 2026, an April 13, 2026, analysis highlighted the White House's National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence, which recommends that Congress consider enabling licensing frameworks or collective rights systems for rights holders to negotiate compensation from AI providers. It also suggests establishing federal protections against the unauthorized distribution or commercial use of AI-generated digital replicas of individuals.
7.  **Meta's $150 Million Content Licensing Deal with News Corp Highlighted**
    A significant multi-year deal between Meta and News Corp, reportedly worth $150 million, was highlighted in an April 17, 2026, article. This agreement allows Meta to use content from News Corp-owned outlets, such as The Wall Street Journal, to train its AI tools.
8.  **EU AI Act Transparency Obligations Deadline Approaches**
    The deadline for the full application of transparency obligations for AI-generated and AI-manipulated content under the EU AI Act is August 2, 2026. An April 8, 2026, report emphasized that compliance planning should be underway for brands and creators operating in the EU.

## Cited sources
1. [brandwatch.com](https://community.brandwatch.com/social-media-management-60/social-media-updates-2026-april-6-10-909)
2. [poynter.org](https://www.poynter.org/business-work/2026/nota-news-companies-cut-contracts-after-plagiarism/)
3. [securityboulevard.com](https://securityboulevard.com/2026/04/the-ai-content-crisis-how-llms-are-draining-media-revenue-and-the-technologies-fighting-back/)
4. [natlawreview.com](https://natlawreview.com/article/picture-ai-enhancements-trademark-search-and-examination)
5. [bakerbotts.com](https://www.bakerbotts.com/thought-leadership/publications/2026/april/ai-legal-watch---april)
6. [dynamisllp.com](https://www.dynamisllp.com/knowledge/ai-disclosure-in-2026-recent-developments-and-practical-steps-for-brands-and-influencers)
